title: Attestation Fast‑Path PRD — Operator Notes & Proposal
content:
Summary:
This is a pragmatic PRD sketch for a low-friction 'attestation fast‑path' aimed at lowering time-to-onboard for customer‑managed networks while preserving an auditable evidence trail. The core idea: provide a lightweight operator experience (UI + compact cryptographic receipt) that satisfies most small/medium onboarding and emergency change flows without forcing full heavyweight evidence bundles every time.

Context & problem:
- Customers adopting Private deployments demand both speed (fast network change, short testing windows) and provable auditability for later forensics or compliance.
- Current proposals in this folder trend toward heavyweight evidence capture (full packet of logs, long retention, large attachments) which increases friction and slows onboarding.
- Platform teams (our customers) tell us they want a path that: 1) lets them approve routine changes quickly, 2) produces minimal machine-verifiable receipts tied to a change, and 3) can be escalated to full evidence only when triggered.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Reduce median time-to-approve routine VPC/operator changes from ~6 hours to <30 minutes for 70% of cases.
- Provide a compact attestation receipt (<= 4 KB) for each approval that is immutable, signed, and queryable for up to 90 days by default.
- Keep storage and egress costs for audit artifacts <25% of current heavy evidence baseline for equivalent volume.
- Integrate with our KMS/HSM flow so receipts can be verified independently by customers.

Non-goals:
- Not replacing full forensic evidence collection for high-risk changes or incidents.
- Not a one-size-fits-all compliance solution for high-security regulated customers (they can opt into full evidence paths).

User personas & primary flows:
- Operator (customer side): needs to approve a VPC route change or certificate rotation fast. Wants a short form, minimal fields, and an optional free-text justification.
- Platform SRE/Operator (Redwood): monitors approvals; can trigger full evidence collection or manual inspection when receipts show anomalies.
- Compliance auditor (post‑hoc): needs to retrieve attestation receipts plus linked artifacts if escalated.

High-level flow (fast‑path):
1) Operator submits change request through Console or API (fields: change_id, operator_id, asset_id, change_type, short_justification, snapshot_hash).
2) System evaluates policy rules (preflight checks): scope, timewindow, operator role, recent change rate.
3) If rules pass, a compact attestation receipt is generated: receipt = {change_id, timestamp, operator_id, policy_version, snapshot_hash, short_justification_hash, signature}. Receipt is signed with Redwood attestation key (customer optional signed-by-customer mode).
4) Receipt is returned to operator and stored in compact ledger (immutable append-only store).
5) If policy flags or rate limits hit, flow escalates to heavyweight approval gate (manual review + full evidence capture).

Receipt design & contents (compact):
- change_id: UUID v4
- timestamp: ISO8601
- actor: operator email / id (hashed for privacy option)
- change_summary_hash: SHA256 of short justification + snapshot metadata
- policy_snapshot_id: reference to policy revision used for automated approval
- signature: platform KMS-signed blob (base64)
- optional: customer_signature (if customer-provided key exists)
- size target: <= 4 KB (text+signature)

Ledger and query model:
- Store receipts in a compact, indexed append-only ledger. Indexes: change_id, operator_id (hashed), asset_id, timestamp.
- Default retention: 90 days (fast-path tier). Cold archive (90d->2y) available as opt-in or triggered by incident escalation.
- Query interface: Console search + API. Support time-range queries, operator-centric queries, change_id lookup.

Approval policy (fast-path rules examples):
- Allowed if operator role in allowlist AND change_type in [route-update, cert-rotation, config-parameter-tweak] AND asset criticality != high AND no conflicting change in last 15m.
- Block and escalate if a change touches 'control-plane' assets or exceeds risk thresholds.

Escalation triggers (examples):
- Multiple fast-path changes affecting same asset within short window.
- Snapshot_hash mismatch to expected baseline.
- Operator has >N reverts in 7d.

Operator UX considerations (notes/to-do):
- Short form with clear labels: what changed, why, rollback plan (optional), expected downtime window.
- Provide a human-friendly summary plus a machine-representation (receipt).
- On approval, show link to downloadable signed receipt and 'Add supporting evidence' button (deferred).
- Visual indicator in Console for 'fast-path approved' vs 'full-evidence required'.

Security & compliance notes:
- Use customer KMS keys for customer-signed receipts (HSM-backed recommended).
- Ensure signature verification code is available to customers (open-source verifier + docs).
- Maintain tamper-evidence by anchoring ledger checkpoints into a Merkle root scheme we publish daily (or per-batch).
- PII minimization: operator identifiers can be hashed or pseudonymized in receipts; provide a mapping service accessible to customer org admins only.

Retention & cost model:
- Default fast-path retention 90 days on hot ledger. After 90 days, receipts expire from hot storage; optionally moved to cold archive for 2 years at lower cost.
- Heavy evidence artifacts (full logs, packet captures) stored only when escalated; chargeable add-on or planned into Dedicated contracts.

API surface (sketch):
- POST /v1/private/attestations/submit -> returns {receipt, status}
- GET /v1/private/attestations/{change_id} -> receipt
- GET /v1/private/attestations?operator_id=...&from=...&to=... -> list
- POST /v1/private/attestations/{change_id}/escalate -> triggers full-evidence pipeline

Open questions / risks (todo list):
- Legal: Is a compact receipt acceptable for customers in regulated sectors as evidence? Need Legal sign-off on 'fast-path' classification.
- Forensics: How to guarantee snapshot_hash integrity if customer does not upload full baseline? Need a minimal snapshot protocol.
- Key management: customer-signed receipts introduce KMS rotation complexities. Policy for key rotation + re-signing?
- Replay & tamper-resistance: frequency of Merkle anchoring vs. cost trade-offs.
- UX: how to communicate risk to operators so they don't overuse fast-path.

Implementation roadmap (rough):
- Phase 0 (2 sprints): API + minimal Console flow, compact receipt generation, append-only store prototype, basic policy engine.
- Phase 1 (4 sprints): KMS integration, signature verification tooling, Console UX polish, retention lifecycle.
- Phase 2 (4 sprints): Merkle anchoring + audit export, escalation workflows (full-evidence pipeline), pricing model.
- Phase 3: customer-signed keyflow, deeper compliance features, configurable retention per org.

Success metrics (tracking):
- Time-to-approve median for fast-path flows
- % of changes using fast-path vs full evidence
- Number of escalations per 1000 fast-path approvals (target <2%)
- Storage cost per 1000 receipts vs baseline

Next steps / immediate action items:
- Get Legal and Security alignment on fast-path evidence sufficiency (owner: Maya).
- Prototype receipt format + create verifier library (owner: Liam Chen, eng-applied-ml).
- Prepare short Console mockups for operator flow (owner: Asha, design).
- Schedule pilot with 2 existing Dedicated customers for real-world feedback (owner: Noah).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the UX optimistic but don’t hide risk. Inline warnings for >N changes/day would help.
- Consider an automated 'rollback snapshot' creation on fast-path approvals to lower forensic costs later.

References & inspiration:
- Compact attestation papers (industry drafts), our prior: attestation-lifecycle-slimline-prd-concepts.md, customer-network-consent-flow-and-tiny-audit-prd-wip.json in the same folder.

Document status: initial product sketch — lots of open questions. Share with Security & Legal next week, then iterate into a fuller PRD.
